questions.question: What three things do plants need to grow, and why does a plant need each one?
questions.expected_answer: Plants need light, water and air. Light gives them the energy to make food in their leaves. Water keeps them firm, carries minerals and is used to make food. Air is taken in through tiny holes in the leaves and is also used to make food.

questions.question: Describe what happens to a bean plant kept in a dark cupboard for two weeks, and explain why.
questions.expected_answer: It grows long, thin and floppy with small, pale yellow leaves. Without light it cannot make food, so it uses up the food stored in its seed while stretching up to find light, and it becomes weak and will die.

questions.question: What is a fair test? Use the bean plants as an example.
questions.expected_answer: A fair test changes only one thing and keeps everything else the same, so you know what caused the result. In the bean test, all plants had the same kind of plant, soil and pot, and only light, or only water, or only air was taken away from one plant.
